# The budget framework {.unnumbered}

*This chapter describes the generic, region-agnostic mass-balance framework. The
theory and tooling here apply to any control volume in any SCHISM-AED run; the
Pioneer application follows in the [next chapter](15-pioneer-estuary.qmd).*

The framework lives in
[`analytics/nutrient_budget/`](../../../analytics/nutrient_budget/). It is
**transferable** — point it at any run and control volume; it has no hard-coded
run paths.

## The mass balance

Given a control volume (CV) — a set of mesh elements — and a tracer group
(currently total nitrogen), the framework assembles a six-term budget:

$$
\frac{dM}{dt} = B + C + D + E + F + \text{residual}
$$

| Term | Meaning | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| A | storage $M(t)$ and $dM/dt$ | scribed state variables + layer height |
| B | internal sinks (denitrification + anammox) | 3D rate diagnostics |
| C | atmospheric flux | `*_atm` sheet diagnostics |
| D | sediment–water interface flux | `*_swi` / `*_dsf` diagnostics |
| E | net boundary exchange | `flux.out` over `fluxflag.prop` regions |
| F | river point sources | `vsource.th` × `msource.th` |

The `residual` is the closure error. In a well-posed budget it stays near zero;
a systematic drift signals a missing or mis-signed term — which is exactly what
the step-by-step checks in [Conservation Testing](16-conservation-testing.qmd)
are designed to catch.

## The `core/` package

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `budget.py` | CLI entry point — runs the full six-term budget |
| `tracer_groups.py` | tracer-pool registry (the nitrogen bundle, signs) |
| `geometry.py` | hgrid I/O, element areas, NetCDF concat, node→element averaging |
| `integrators.py` | Terms A–D (storage, rates, surface fluxes) |
| `boundary_fluxes.py` | `flux.out` parser + Term E aggregator |
| `point_sources.py` | `source_sink` / `vsource` / `msource` → Term F |
| `report.py` | CSV / PNG / HTML writers |
| `build_cv.py` | define a CV from a polygon + fluxflag regions |

## Running the budget CLI

```bash
python core/budget.py \
    --region       <region>.yaml \
    --tracer-group nitrogen \
    --outputs-dir  <run>/outputs \
    --hgrid        <run>/hgrid.gr3 \
    --param-nml    <run>/param.nml \
    --n-stacks     14 \
    --output-dir   ./_outputs/<name>
```

The `--region` YAML names the CV element list and the bounding `fluxflag.prop`
regions; building one is covered in the [next chapter](15-pioneer-estuary.qmd).

## What a budget run produces

Every run writes a self-contained set of outputs to its `--output-dir`:

| Output | Contents |
|---|---|
| `budget_timeseries.csv` | every term, time-indexed |
| `budget_stacked.png` | instantaneous mass-balance, stacked area |
| `budget_cumulative.png` | cumulative time-integrals (tonnes N) |
| `report.html` | a narrated walk-through with the plots embedded, the closure check, and sanity notes |

The **`report.html`** is the primary artefact to read — it bundles the plots,
the closure residual, and commentary into one self-contained page. Rather than
reproduce its content here, the [Pioneer estuary chapter](15-pioneer-estuary.qmd)
embeds and links a real example.

## Reading a closure check

The diagnostic plots compare the observed storage change against the sum of the
accounted-for terms. When the budget closes, the two track each other and the
residual stays near zero; a growing residual points to a missing or mis-signed
term. Volume and salinity are the cheapest checks, because they are conservative
and well constrained — they are the first things to look at before trusting the
nutrient terms.

## Supporting diagnostics

Beyond the headline budget, the toolkit ships a set of **diagnostic scripts**
that interrogate each term independently — the checks needed to trust (or
distrust) a closure. They live in
[`pioneer_region_flux/diagnostics/`](../../../analytics/pioneer_region_flux/diagnostics/)
and target a run by name (`--run 002|003`). In brief:

- **conservation checks** — observed storage change vs source + boundary, per
  variable (`conservation_check.py`, `global_balance.py`);
- **conservative-tracer benchmarks** — AED `TRC` vs SCHISM-native `GEN`
  (`tr1_vs_gen1_compare.py`);
- **transect assessments** — independent edge-flux reconstruction and
  positive/negative/net breakdowns at the mouth (`edge_flux_reconstruction.py`,
  `check_flux_upwind.py`, `mouth_edge_classification.py`);
- **source & connectivity checks** — injection-ratio and wet/dry diagnostics at
  the river source (`src3_dry_rat_check.py`, `upper_river_connectivity.py`);
- **per-variable accounts** — a 20-variable gallery of source vs transect vs
  storage (`per_variable_plots.py`).

These are applied step by step in
[Conservation Testing](16-conservation-testing.qmd).

## Nutrient Budget regions

The boundary term depends entirely on how the domain is partitioned into **flux
regions**. `fluxflag.prop` labels every element with a region number, and SCHISM
reports the tracer transport across the interface between regions of adjacent
number into `flux.out`. These transects are the pre-configured "gates" through
which a control volume exchanges mass with the rest of the domain.

![The `fluxflag.prop` regions across the model domain — the pre-configured budget gates. Source: `analytics/pioneer_region_flux/diagnostics/inspect_fluxflag.py`](../../assets/images/budget/fluxflag_map_full.png){#fig-fluxflag-full}

A control volume is then assembled from elements bounded by these regions. The
Pioneer setup uses a simplified region set that makes the mouth (3↔2) transect
explicit — defining such a region and reading its budget is the subject of the
[Pioneer Estuary](15-pioneer-estuary.qmd) chapter.
